idiom_name: object literal (or class) satisfying the collaborator interface by structural typing
implementation_notes: TypeScript's structural type system means the test does not have to declare conformance: an object literal with the members the SUT calls is accepted wherever the collaborator interface is expected, so the test's own object is the double with no implements clause and no framework. A class implementing the interface is the alternative when several tests in a suite share the recording; jest.fn() supplies typed call recording and replaces the hand-written shunt once arguments, call counts or canned answers must be asserted. The literal form stays justified while the observable contract is one or two members and the assertions read the recorded array directly.
pitfalls: Excess property checks reject object literals carrying members the interface does not declare, so a stray helper on the literal fails compilation while the same object assigned through a variable passes.
jest.fn() without a type argument accepts any signature, so a drift between the mock and the collaborator interface is not caught at compile time.
Narrowing the collaborator interface by marking members optional just to satisfy a literal hides required behaviour from production callers; narrow the SUT's dependency instead.
